description: Reads the rows of one Notion data source (a table inside a database), with an optional filter, sort order, property allowlist, page size and cursor. Each row is {id, url, created_time, last_edited_time, properties}, with properties as plain values keyed by property name. Filter and sorts are passed to Notion as written, in Notion's query JSON; notion_get_database lists the property names and types they refer to. The result is {results, has_more, next_cursor}, with the same shape when there are no results. has_more true means more results exist than this page holds, and next_cursor is the cursor argument that returns them. With view_id in place of data_source_id, the rows are a saved view's, in its own filter and sort order, and each row is its id alone, which is what Notion's view query returns; notion_get_page reads a row's properties. A view query's results stay cached for 15 minutes; total_count is the number of rows it matched, and incomplete true means Notion's 10,000-row cache cut them short.

account.description: Optional email address of the connected account to use (e.g. 'user@gmail.com'). If omitted, the default account is used.

cursor.description: The next_cursor value from an earlier call with the same arguments. Returns the page of results after that one. Absent for the start of the list.

data_source_id.description: The data source's Notion id, with or without dashes, or a Notion URL that contains it (the id is read from the URL).

filter.description: A Notion filter object, sent unchanged. Example: {"property": "Status", "status": {"equals": "Done"}}; compound filters use {"and": [...]} or {"or": [...]}. Notion's filter reference documents the condition each property type takes. Absent returns every row.

page_size.description: How many results one call returns, from 1 to 100. Default 25. A full page comes back with has_more true and a next_cursor for the rest.

properties.description: Property names to keep in each row. Absent keeps every property. Names that a row does not have are left out of that row.

sorts.description: A list of Notion sort objects, sent unchanged, applied in order. Example: [{"property": "Due", "direction": "ascending"}] or [{"timestamp": "last_edited_time", "direction": "descending"}].

view_id.description: A database view's id, or a database URL whose ?v= names the view. Takes the place of data_source_id; filter, sorts and properties are not taken with it.

name: notion-mcp__notion_query_data_source
